sections.h2: Tax Office location and phone numbers
sections.html:
The office is inside the Pamlico County Courthouse, 202 Main Street, Bayboro, NC 28515. Letters go to Box 538 there, and the counter is staffed weekdays from eight until five.

One office does the work of both assessor and collector. It lists property, sets values, records ownership changes and collects current and past-due tax. The county commissioners appoint the Tax Administrator. The office email is tax.office@pamlicocounty.org, and three direct lines split the work.

  • Listing, for personal and business property: 252-745-3105
  • Collections and payment plans: 252-745-4125
  • Land Records: 252-745-3791
  • Fax: 252-745-4042

The office's key dates run from January to September and repeat each year. Ownership is fixed on January 1 and bills are due September 1.

  • January 1: ownership is declared as of this date.
  • January 5: the deadline for paying with no interest.
  • January 31: listing period ends.
  • April: the Board of Equalization and Review begins hearing appeals.
  • May 31: the deadline to settle overdue tax before the newspaper ad.
  • June 1: final day for exemption and exclusion applications.
  • July: bills go out in the mail.
  • September 1: bills come due.

After a missed January date the state adds 2% starting January 6, and from February 1 interest grows by three-fourths of one percent per month or part of one.

The last reappraisal took effect January 1, 2020. Call 252-745-3105 for the date of the next one.

The county calls its schedule the Octennial Plan, after the state's eight-year limit. Values track the market as of the last reappraisal date and are adjusted only at the next one. The assessor handles more than 17,000 real property parcels, plus business personal property, mobile homes and aircraft, and all of it must be valued by the same standard.

The county rate is 0.7000 for 2026, up from 0.645 in 2025. Town and fire district charges stack on that, which makes location decisive.

Pamlico County has 12 tax districts, and the money pays for schools, roads, police and fire protection. The county's worked example multiplies a $100,000 value by the town and fire rate per hundred dollars for a house in Bayboro in the Triangle Fire District. Call the Tax Office to confirm which rates apply to your parcel.

Other towns are Mesic, Minnesott, Stonewall, Grantsboro, Alliance and Arapahoe, which has a town rate of 0.

The county column moved from 0.645 to 0.7000, and most fire districts moved up as well. Town rates mostly held still.

  • Grants/Slv. Hill Fire: 0.08 in 2025, 0.1100 in 2026
  • Olympia Fire: 0.0760 in 2025, 0.1100 in 2026
  • Reelsboro Fire: 0.0821 in 2025, 0.1130 in 2026
  • FL / Whort Fire: 0.0613 in 2025, 0.0810 in 2026
  • Goose Creek Island: 0.06 in 2025, 0.0700 in 2026
  • Bayboro and Vandemere town rates: unchanged at 0.27 and 0.23

A house on Goose Creek Island, one near Reelsboro and one in Bayboro can therefore draw very different bills from the same county value. Ask for the rate sheet that matches your district before you estimate what a buyer will carry.

Put the request for a hearing in writing and deliver it to the board's clerk before the panel adjourns. The Tax Administrator serves as that clerk, at P.O. Box 538, Bayboro, NC 28515.

The board meets in the spring, beginning in April and adjourning in May, and the county's real estate appeal form is marked for a January through May window. You must show that the value or location was wrong or that the property was taxed in error. A taxpayer who loses at the board can go to the Property Tax Commission in Raleigh by sending written notice within a month of the mailing date, 30 days to be exact.

The forms page carries applications and instructions for the elderly or disabled exclusion, the circuit breaker deferment and the disabled veteran exemption. It also has forms for present use value, a property tax exemption and a business property exemption.

  • The state's income ceiling for the 2026 tax year is $38,800.
  • Under the elderly or disabled program, the larger of $25,000 and half the appraised value comes off the taxable amount.
  • For a disabled veteran the first $45,000 of value is excluded, with no age or income test.
  • Circuit breaker owners pay at most 4.0% or 5.0% of income, based on how income compares with the ceiling, and the remainder is deferred.

Applications must reach the office by June 1. Call the Listing line to ask for forms.

sections.h2: Selling with the tax bill outstanding
sections.html:
The bill follows the parcel, so closing must clear it. The yearly tax becomes a lien when property is listed, and penalties, interest and costs ride along with it.

Before picking a closing date, call Collections at 252-745-4125 for the balance. Overdue accounts get advertised after May 31. Where the county forecloses, the sale happens at the courthouse door. The seller also pays the deed stamp tax, $1 for each $500, at the deeds office ahead of recording. A closing attorney usually collects both from the proceeds.

A cash sale skips lender underwriting and appraisal, but it does not skip the tax payoff. Ask for the balance in writing so the closing agent can pay it from your proceeds.

Start with the Land Records line at 252-745-3791 to confirm the parcel record matches your deed. Next ask Collections for the balance on every open year. Then check your district on the rate sheet so you know what a buyer will carry. If you receive an exclusion or deferment, ask the Listing line how a sale affects it, since circuit breaker owners repay deferred tax when they sell. Finally, hand the payoff figures to your closing attorney so they can be paid from proceeds.

Taking these steps before the sign goes up avoids delays at the closing table, whether the buyer is using a loan or paying cash.

Pamlico is a small, mostly owner-occupied county with an estimated 12,758 residents in 2025, 4.0% above 2020. Owners live in 82.9% of homes, and the middle value among them is $216,800. Median rent is $752. The county counts 5,456 households in 7,610 housing units, and building permits totaled 97 in 2025. District lines weigh heavily on a bill, since the rate page lists eight fire districts plus Goose Creek Island.

faqs.q: When are Pamlico County property taxes due?
faqs.a: September 1. Mailing happens in July, and January 5 is the final interest-free day.

faqs.q: Which number reaches the Pamlico County tax staff?
faqs.a: Call Collections at 252-745-4125 for payments and payment plans, or Listing at 252-745-3105 for personal and business property. The office is at 202 Main Street, Bayboro.

faqs.q: What is the Pamlico County tax rate?
faqs.a: The county rate is 0.7000 for 2026, with separate town and fire district figures added on top. Call the office to confirm your parcel's combination.

faqs.q: When can I appeal my Pamlico County assessment?
faqs.a: In spring. The Board of Equalization and Review opens in April, and the written request must reach the clerk before the board adjourns in May.

faqs.q: What is the deadline for tax relief applications in Pamlico County?
faqs.a: June 1 for exemption and exclusion applications. Use the Listing line, 252-745-3105, for forms.
